name: Frontend Engineering
guidance: Before implementation create docs/delivery-concept.md: Visual thesis (brand, audience, mood, typography/color/spacing); Content plan (one job per section and a primary CTA); Interaction plan (real control behavior); Evidence (confirmed facts, unknown facts, assets, source/license and review limits).

Prioritize user assets and confirmed business facts. Where imagery or context is missing, call research_sources with target images/context and payload query plus language. Choose intentional imagery; never invent image URLs, addresses, prices, founding dates, testimonials or business contacts.

Build a distinctive brand composition with purposeful type, restrained spacing and a dominant relevant visual when imagery serves the mission. Avoid repeated generic card grids; preserve an existing design system when provided. Write concise specific copy in the user language.
Implement semantic responsive HTML, meaningful alt text, keyboard focus and every requested interaction. Do not put delivery-process commentary or internal review labels into the product UI.

Validate the actual deliverable, assets and primary controls. Structural checks and inspect_result do not prove visual quality. Without a real browser/vision tool, report desktop/mobile and visual review as pending in delivery notes; never claim professionally reviewed.
Refine hierarchy, image crop, contrast, mobile layout and copy after rendered-page review. Publish facts, sources/license credits and tested behavior separately from review still pending.
completion_checks: Delivery concept exists with confirmed facts separated from unknowns and a coherent brand/content/interaction direction.
The requested page and controls exist; attached assets take priority and any external assets have a real retrieved source, author and applicable license/credits.
Delivery states what was actually tested and whether browser and visual reviews are pending; no model statement is presented as tool evidence.
